motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to table the Scenic Mountain Phase C site plan until the next meeting, directing the applicant to return with elevations that dilbrentiate between the individual units, an updated parking plan, and an amenity plan with increased connectivity as discussed. Councilmember Love seconded the motion. Those voting aye: Donna Burnham, Melissa Clark, Colby Curtis, and Carolyn Love. The motion passedwith a unanimous vote. 16. PRELIMINARY PLAT AMENDMENT 16.4. MOTION - Brylee Farms Preliminary Plat Amendment Mr. Kane presented the item. Brylee Farms includes Phase A single-family and Phase B townhome residential developments. The preliminary plats for these phases were approved in 2018 and2019, respectively. Phase A is being developed by Fieldstone Homes and Phase B is being developed by Concord Homes. The developers desire to merge the homeowners' associations (HOAs) that will oversee the open space and amenities in the developments into one master HOA. The proposed amendment changes the park space in Phase A from aplayground to a swimming pool, clubhouse, active lawn space, and parking areas. The proposed amendment in Phase B moves the separate tot lot to the large park area, leaving the former tot lot area as improved open space; removes the sport court above the underground retention to leave the land as improved park space for informal sport activities; and expands amenities at the primary amenity area with pickleball courts, a large playground, pavilion, and parking areas. Based on the proposed open spacs and amenities amendment, the new plan would achieve 1,003 points in total between the two phases where 737 points are required. The applicants are seeking to amend the preliminary plat for the two phases with regards to the open space and amenities. There are no proposed changes to the number of lots, density, or right- of-way configurations. Multifamily projects are required to include a clubhouse and swimming pool (EMMC 17.25.050). These elements cannot count toward the amenity points as they are required for this development type. The proposed pool is sized at2,000 square feet, exceeding the size minimum of 1,268 square feet by 732 square feet. The proposed pool and clubhouse meet the size requirement of the Phase B development but will be located within Phase A. The amenity area within Phase A is within a quarter-mile distance of all residences in both phases except for twelve torisnhome units in the northwest corner. The amenity area within Phase B is within a quarter-mile distance of all residences in both phases except for six single-family properties in the southwest corner. Per the approved preliminary plat for Phase B, a pedestrian crossing was to be included between the main amenity area and the trail to the west. The Planning Commission held a public hearing on November 10, 2020, to review the preliminary plat amendment application. The Commission unanimously voted, with one absentee, to recommend approval of the preliminary plat amendment with the condition the applicant shall remove two spaces in the center of the row of the parking area on the west side of the primary amenity area in Phase B in order to incorporate a landscape island and pedestrian crossing. During the December 1, 2020, City Council meeting, Councilmembers raised concerns about the proposed location of the clubhouse and pool. The request was tabled with feedback related to the clubhouse and pool location to potentially relocate the pool to the location of lots 69 to 72, swap the amenities between the two phases, or place the pool and clubhouse in a more central location. Councilmember Clark stated that the Municipal Code square footage requirements for clubhouses include all the residential units being served by the clubhouse. She expressed concern that the applicant was counting additional amenity points for the size of the pool, in excess of the requirement, while also desiring for the increased pool size to offset the deficit in the clubhouse size. Applicant representative Matthew Loveland with Fieldstone Homes stated that the project would exceed the required number of amenity points, even if the additional square footage for the pool was not included in the calculations. Mr. Loveland presented a review of the proposal and explained their intention was to partner with Concord Homes to offer grandeur amenities at a reduced HOA assessment to residents of both projects and compared the larger pool and additional amenities to the minimal required amenities for the project. He demonstrated that all the units adhered to the standard for units to be located within a one-quarter mile from a park. He believed that the residents would prefer the increased number of amenities rather than a higher HOA assessment with the amenities specifically required for their unit type to be located slightly closer to their homes. He said that a redesign is not an option due to the progress on the project and other constraints and because they believe their plan is what is best for the community.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 2.05 Employees and Personnel and 2.10 Mayor, and Enacting Chapters 2.16 City Administrator and 2.27 Board Appointment Process. Mr. Cook stated the items requested by the City Council at the previous meeting have been incorporated into the proposed Municipal Code amendment. Councilmember Love requested for the requirement for the City Council to approve amendments to the Policies and Procedures to be included in Municipal Code. Mr. Cook stated the City Council could elect to amend the verbiage in EMMC 2.10.010(E) to o'shall make recommendations to the city council regarding the City's policies and procedures found by the mayor to be necessary for the proper administration of the city council which shall be approved by the city council," to accommodate Councilmember Love's request. He explained that the approval process has always included city council approval; however, cilv council approval may be codified'if desired. Councilmember Love expressed concem regarding the mayor recommending to the city council a process to hire a new city administrator and advocated for the establishment of a set process that included the City posting the position and accepting applications. She stated her support for the City's practice to implement succession plans and hiring from within; however, she believes as a government entity transparency and due diligence are important and that posting and interviewing should be required accordingly. Mr. Cook stated that a committee and complex hiring process might be necessary when seeking an applicant regionally; however, that process may not be appropriate in all instances. He expressed concern regarding implementing a complex, unnecessary process that may require a future City Council to hold a special session to amend delaying the hiring of a new City Administrator. Councilmember Love clarified that she does not desire to codifr a specific, complex hiring process, but desires for the hiring of the position to require posting and accepting application. Mr. Cook stated that his understanding of the inclusion of the proposed amended verbiage that "the process shall, at a minimum, include public noticing for the position," in EMMC 2.16.020 indicated the position would be posted externally and would necessitate accepting applications. Councilmember Love requested clarification regarding the public notification process and posting locations. Mr. Cook stated that if the City does not have an internal applicant in mind for the position, the City would likely hire a consultant to assist with recruiting applicants. Ms. Kofoed recommended for the wording to include the posting of the position to clariff the position would be posted in the applicable locations. Councilmember Clark inquired if Councilmember Love desired for the line "the mayor shall recommend to the city council a process to hire a new city administrator," to be stricken from EMMC 2.16.020. Councilmember Love stated she would support the retention of the line if the requirement to post the position were also required. Councilmember Curtis suggested to amend the verbiage to "the mayor may recommend to the city council a process to hire a new city administrator." Councilmember Clark expressed her preference for "shall" rather than "may" and concuned that the position should be required to be posted externally as it will resolve most of her concems. Discussion ensued debated whether the standards should include "shall" or "may." Councilmember Curtis expressed concern that a mayor could include the proposed process and the name of his or her recoirmended applicant as items on the same agenda. Councilmember Clark concurred with Councilmember Curtis' concerns and recommended for the process to be determined prior to the submission of the name of an individual for consideration. Councilmember Love stated she felt the intention for the hiring process to proceed with the selection of the presentation of a name for consideration was clearly understood in the proposal. Councilmember Burnham concurred with Councilmember Love that the order of the process was clear as written; however, she did not object to additional language to prescribe that the establishment of the process was prior to the naming and presentation of the mayor's recommended applicant. Discussion ensued regarding verbiage specifications to ensure the process proceeds as requested by the City Council. Councilmember Clark noted that other cities include a term of employment, an annual performance review of the City Administration performed by the Mayor, and a six-month term in which a newly elected mayor may not remove the existing City Administrator. Councilmember Curtis expressed concem about implementing standards that offered an unreasonable level ofjob protection for a City Administrator that could prevent the necessary or appropriate removal of a City Administrator. Discussion ensued regarding the inclusion of protections against a new mayor replacing the City Administrator for political or personal reasons. Councilmember Love stated that the removal of the City Administrator required the approval of the Mayor and the City Council. Mr. Cook stated that the proposal provides that "the city administrator may be removed and the contract of the city administrator may be terminated by a majority vote of the city council with the mayor acting as a voting member of the city council," which provides protection to the City Administrator due to the requirement for a vote by at least four of the six members and the contract includes a six-month severance package. He explained that the position is intended to be subject to at-will employee conditions. He stated that an annual review would be appropriate and could be beneficial to both the City and the City Administrator regarding salary, duties, and performance. Councilmember Clark stated the requirement of a majority vote resolved her concerns regarding protecting the City Administrator. Councilmember Clark requested for applications to be provided to the City Council prior to the publishing of the packet materials to the public. Mr. Cook clarified that the proposed standards require for the mayor to provide the name and application or resume, if available, of board appointees to the City Council not less than five days prior to public noticing. Councilmember Curtis recommended for the standards to allow for the mayor or designee to be allowed to provide the materials to the City Council. Discussion ensued regarding the timeframe for the notification to the City Council prior to public notification in order to address Council concems regarding potential appointees to prevent the public embarrassment of the individuals. Councilmember Clark requested for the City Council to be provided the names of possible appointees two weeks prior to the City Council meeting when the names will be announced. Ms. Kofoed stated that the timing of when the City Council can be provided the names of individuals to fill appointments depends upon when applications are received, and staff is willing to comply with the timeframe stipulated by the Council. Mr. Cook clarified that the standards under discussion exclude the Planning Commission which is under a separate City statute and regulated by State statute. Councilmember Love clarified that the City Council only desires to review the applicants selected by the Mayor to fill board vacancies, not all applicants. Mr. Cook expressed concern that the request for two weeks to review appointments will delay filling board positions but might be preferred by the Council. Councilmember Clark clarified her request for a two-week timeframe is in part due to the appointments occurring at the end of the year around the holidays and suggested for the process to be amended to accommodate the two-week timeframe if necessary. Councilmember Love requested for an amendment to the Municipal Code requirements for the Planning Commission to be brought to the City Council and advocated for the same standards to apply for the Planning Commission as other boards. Discussion ensued regarding the desired timeframe for the Mayor to provide the City Councilmembers with possible appointments for various boards. Ms. Kofoed inquired if an exception would be allowed for individuals willing to fill board positions that have not applied. Mr. Cook explained the proposed verbiage requires for the application or resume to be provided "if available" to allow for appointments for individuals that did not apply. if Mayor Westmoreland requested clarification regarding the impact to the processing timeframe the City Council has objections to the individual proposed by the mayor. Councilmember Love stated she believes the timeframe would reset and recommended allowing a five-day prior to notification time period rather than two weeks due to. the increase to the overall appointment process timeframe. Discussion ensued regarding the desired timeframe and the impact of the City Council objection to a recommended appointee and the time required for the Mayor to receive feedback from all the individual Councilmembers in order to prevent the public embarrassment of an appointee. Councilmember Clark stated that although she did not feel that there would be frequent objections to the Mayor's recommended appointees, this process was a kind way to conduct the business of the City. Discussion ensued regarding potential scenarios that would impact the desired timeframe. Councilmember Clark conceded to retain the timeframe as proposed for the Mayor to provide the City Council the name of potential appointees not less than five days prior to publicly noticing the possible appointment. Councilmembers Clark and Love recommended tabling the item to allow time for the requested changes to return to the City Council for approval at a future meeting. Discussion ensued regarding the desired requirements for the frequency of the City Administrator's reviews with the Mayor. Mr. Cook recommended once per calendar year to coincide with the contract date. Councilmember Burnham inquired regarding the impact of delaying the ordinance approval to the upcoming 202I board appointments. Councilmember Clark stated that the Mayor could elect to follow the changes proposed by the City Council even though the proposal has not been approved. Mr. Cook noted that the changes requested by the City Council in this meeting only require the addition of a few words to the proposed amendments presented in the meeting. He clarified that the desired changes to the Planning Commission standards would need to be noticed separately and could not be added to the proposal for this item on a future agenda. He recommended passing this item and including an amendment to the Planning Commission standards at a future meeting. Councilmember Love requested for the City Council to be able to review the amended verbiage prior to passing the item.
motions.motion: Councilmember Love moved to table an ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code chapters 2.05 Employees and Personnel and 2.10 Mayor, and Enacting Chapters 2.16 City Administrator and 2.27 Board Appointment Process in order to allow Mr. Cook to implement the requested amendments in accordance with the following proposed recommendations discussed in the meeting: 1. EMMC 2.10.010(E) "Shall make recommendations to the city council regarding the City's policies and procedures found by the mayor to be necessaryfor the proper administration of the city council which shall be approved by the city council;" 2. EMMC 2.16.020 "The process shall, at the minimum, include posting the position and accepting applications ; " 3. The line "the mayor shall recommend to the city council a process to hire a new city administrator," to be strickenfrom EMMC 2.16.020; 4. The mayor shall conduct an annual perbrmance review of the City Administration in coruelations with the date of the employment contract; and 5. A designee may provide the City Council with the name and application or resume, dprovided, of the Mayor's recommended board appointees. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. Those voting aye: Donna Burnham, Melissa Clark, Colby Curtis, and Carolyn Love. The motion passed with a unanimous vote.
